reading: The 3x3 input becomes a 3x3 grid of blocks; each block whose position is a foreground cell of the input holds a copy of the input, the rest are empty.
why: block (i,j) of the output equals the input iff input cell (i,j) is foreground, else it is all background
invariants: the input pattern inside every copied block

reading: The 6x3 input is a vertically periodic pattern; the output continues the pattern to 9 rows and recolours 1 to 2.

slots.pattern: the smallest vertical period of the input rows (2, 4 or 3 rows)

why: output row r equals input row (r mod period) with 1 replaced by 2

reading: The objects standing on the bottom row are taken left to right and chained diagonally from the top-left corner: each next object's top-left cell sits on the previous object's bottom-right cell, the later object drawn on top.

slots.subject: every object, ordered by leftmost column
slots.step: next object's top-left = previous object's bottom-right corner (overlap one cell, later overwrites)

why: each object keeps its shape and colour; consecutive objects share exactly the corner cell, which takes the later colour

reading: One 3x3 single-colour shape is the exemplar; each small fragment of another colour lying next to it (gap 1) marks a direction, and the exemplar is repeated in that direction every 4 cells in the fragment's colour until the border.

slots.unit: the exemplar: the largest object (3x3 shape)
slots.direction: from the exemplar towards each fragment (orthogonal or diagonal)

why: each fragment is a part of the first copy; all copies have the exemplar's shape and lie on the ray at spacing 4

reading: A lattice of copies of one tile is corrupted by noise; the output replaces every tile by the cell-wise majority over all tiles and clears all noise outside the tiles.

slots.unit: the repeated tile (same-size boxes on a regular row/column lattice)
slots.value: per tile position, the most common colour across all tile copies
slots.rest: cells outside the tile boxes cleared to background

why: every output tile is identical and equals the per-cell majority of the input tiles; nothing outside the tiles is non-background

reading: The 3x3 input becomes a 3x3 grid of blocks; each block at a foreground position holds the colour-inverted input (foreground and background swapped), the others are empty.

slots.extent: fg cells of the input pick the blocks
slots.unit: the input with foreground and background swapped (foreground colour on input's background cells)

why: block (i,j) equals the inverted input iff input cell (i,j) is foreground, else all background

reading: On a grid of cells cut by lines, every two same-coloured blocks on one row or column of cells are joined: the background cells between them take their colour, the grid lines stay.
why: a background cell is filled with colour c exactly when the nearest non-line coloured cells on both sides along its row or its column are both c; line cells never change

reading: Separator lines cut the grid into 3x3 panels of 3x3 cells; the one panel with 4 coloured cells (others have 5) is enlarged: each output panel is filled with the colour of the matching cell of that panel, or left empty.

slots.source: the odd panel: the panel with the fewest non-background cells
slots.map: source cell (i,j) -> whole panel (i,j) filled with that cell's colour (background stays background)

why: every output panel is uniform and equals the colour of the corresponding cell of the sparsest input panel

reading: Each small plus (centre colour c, four arms colour a) grows into a 5x5 star: arms of colour a reach distance 2, and both diagonals of colour c reach distance 2.

slots.arms: orthogonal rays of length 2 in the arm colour
slots.diagonals: diagonal rays of length 2 in the centre colour

why: every plus becomes the same 5x5 star pattern relative to its centre, colours taken from that plus

reading: Each blob of 1s contains one seed cell of another colour; every 1-cell of the blob whose 8 neighbours are all non-background (the blob's inside) takes the seed colour.

new_rows.name: interior
new_rows.datalog:
inb(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C).
nb0(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, px(Y2, X2, D), D = 0.
nbout(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, !inb(Y2, X2).
interior(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 1, !nb0(Y, X), !nbout(Y, X).

why: within each 8-connected blob, exactly the 1-cells with no background or off-grid neighbour change, and they become the blob's seed colour
